Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Chronic torn ACL. Right lateral knee pain after fall.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst. T1 and T2 hypointense 3 cm lesion in the posterior joint capsule, along the posterior cruciate ligament.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique undersurface tear of the posterior horn.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Complex tear of the body and posterior horn with a dominant horizontal component extending to the root attachment. Mild extrusion of the body.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild chondrosis with high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Moderate chondrosis, with diffuse high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss and areas of full-thickness fissuring in the medial patellar facet

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Chronic complete ACL tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Oblique undersurface tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
2.	Complex tear of the lateral meniscus with a dominant horizontal component and mild extrusion of the body.
3.	Mild lateral and moderate patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.
4.	Chronic complete ACL tear.
5.	3 cm hypointense lesion in the posterior joint capsule, with features consistent with PVNS.

Suženje zglobnog prostora FT zgloba, izraženije u medijalnom dijelu, uz šire zone koštanog
edema medijalnih zglobnih ploha femura i tibije koji se uvlači i u rubne koštane apozicije.
Subhondralno je vidljiva i sitna cistična pregradanja kosti.
Gotovo potpuna denudacija zglobnih ploha medijalnog kompartmenta FT zgloba.
Promjene odgovaraju uznapredovaloj OA sa hondromalacijskim promjenama 4. stupnja. Stanjenje
hrskavica lateralnog kompartmenta uz hondromalaciju 2. stupnja.
Umjereni izljev suprapatelarno.
Prednji križni ligament je povišenog signala u smislu miksoidne degeneracije, potencijalno sa
arealima parcijalne rupture starijeg datuma.
Stražnji križni ligament urednog signala te se prati u kontinuitetu.
Medijalni menisk je izrazito promjenjenog i povišenog intenziteta signala korpusa i stražnjeg roga,
sa ekstruzijom pod MCL za 5 mm - degenerativna ruptura.
Lateralni menisk povišenog signala u smislu degeneracije.
Lateralni kolateralni ligament blaže povišenog intenziteta signala na proksimalnom hvatištu,
moguće uslijed distenzije. Medijalni kolateralni ligamenti normalnog signala. Oba se prate u
kontinuitetu.
Uredan intenzitet signala hvatišta tetive kvadricepsa i patelarnog ligamenta.
Uredna je kongruencija zglobnih tijela femoropatelarnog zgloba. Povišen intenzitet signala
patelarne hrskavice uz fisure te manji edem patele u smislu hondromalacije 4. stupnja. Opsežni rubni osteofiti.
Edem mekih tkiva prepatelarno i pretibijalno uz fibrozno promijenjenu prepatelarnu burzu. Edem
Hoffine masti.
Bisagasta septirana poplitealna cista dimenzija oko 2x1.5 cm.
Manja ganglion cista uz tetivu m. popliteusa.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Moderate degenerative subchondral cystic changes are present at the trochlea, lateral greater than medial. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Mild, diffuse synovial proliferation. No loose intra-articular bodies are seen. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a horizontal tear along the posterior horn extending to the root attachment. Mild extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is tearing of the inner margin along the body and posterior horn. No extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is full-thickness cartilage fissuring at the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring at the patella diffusely. Severe cartilage loss is present at the trochlea diffusely with subchondral cystic changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild tendinosis.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:


1. Medial and lateral meniscal tear.

2. Tricompartmental chondrosis, most prominent at the trochlea.

3. Mild quadriceps tendinosis.

4. Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

- In the medial compartment, there is horizontal tear from anterior to posterior horn. Complex tear with gap 5 mm at posterior horn. 
 There is diffuse high grade chondrosis (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along weight-baring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is subchondral edema. Subchondral bone cyst is present. Osteophytes are present.  
 - The lateral compartment, contusional injury at anterior horn of meniscus.  
  
 - The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial, lateral patellar facets, medial and lateral trochleas. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 - In the intercondylar notch,  
 ACL high grade partial tear.  
 the posterior cruciate ligaments are intact.  
  
 - MCL;  
 superficial; intact 
 deep; high grade injury 
 - LCL; high grade injury at femoral attachment 
 - Popliteus tendon; low grade injury at femoral attachment 
  
  
 - The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of left knee effusion with synovitis is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion. - LCL; high grade injury at femoral attachment 
 - ACL high grade partial tear.  
 -- Some amount of left knee effusion with synovitis

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain for 2 months after fall. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Small heterogenous T2 hyperintense lesion at the medial femoral metaphysis, consistent with a nonaggressive chondroid lesion.

JOINT SPACE:
Large joint effusion with synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Markedly diminutive, related to prior debridement, with extensive complex tearing of the remnant meniscus and maceration of the body.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage denudation in the weightbearing compartment with broad areas of full-thickness cartilage loss, large marginal osteophytes and subchondral marrow edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Inner margin tearing of the body and anterior horn. No extrusion. 
Lateral compartment cartilage: High-grade chondrosis with superimposed full-thickness fissuring at the weightbearing lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau with large marginal spurs.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade chondrosis with superimposed full-thickness fissuring, most prominent at the lateral patellar facet and lateral trochlea, and large marginal spurs.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Chronic high-grade ACL tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact. Bowing with reactive periligamentous edema, related to meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with associated enthesopathy. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. Multilobulated ganglion cyst extending into the popliteus sheath. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis, most advanced in the medial compartment.
2.	Markedly diminutive medial meniscus, related to prior debridement, with extensive complex tearing of the remnant meniscus and maceration of the body.
3.	Chronic high-grade tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).
4.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with associated enthesopathy.
5.	Moderate right knee effusion.

Na seriji MR presjeka lijevog koljena vidi se koštani edem medijalnog kondila femura i platoa
tibije uz potpuno reduciranu debljinu artikulacijske hrskavice medijalnog kondila femura i platoa
tibije te vidljivu manju zonu subhondralnog edema posteriornog dijela kondila femura
(hondromalacija IV. stupnja). Masivni osteofiti medijalnog kondila femura i platoa tibije. Uredna
je morfologija i intenziteti signala lateralnog kolateralnog kompleksa, stražnjeg križnog
ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarnog ligamenta i tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Blaža mukoidna degeneracija prednjeg križnog ligamenta uz vidljive sitne cistične degenerativne
promjene pri tibijalnom hvatištu.
Periligamentarni edem MCL u sklopu OA promjena.
Kompleksna ruptura stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska na degenerativnoj podlozi. Vidi se defekt
dijela tijela medijalnog meniska uz ekstruziju istog.
Kompleksna ruptura stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska (horizontalna i dominantno
longitudinalna).
Vide se fissure medijalne fasete patele koje zahvaćaju >50% površine (hondromalacija III.
stupnja).
Značajno je reducirana debljina artikulacijske hrskavice medijalne i lateralne trohleje femura.
Manja zona subhondralnog koštanog edema medijalne trohleje femura.
Hondromalacija II./III. stupnja lateralnog platoa tibije.
Opsežan izljev u koljenu, dominantno u suprapatelarnom recessusu. Ne nalazi se poplitealne
(Bakerove) ciste.
Edem Hoffine masti - ddg. impigement.
Unutar masnog tkiva, s dorzalne strane distalne dijametafize femura vidi se cistična lezija
promjera 21 mm.
Manja količina lokulirane tekućine unutar lateraelnog dijela m. popliteusa prema
mišićno-tetivnom prijelazu te između m. popliteusa i lateralna glave m. gastrocnemiusa.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. Large complex popliteal cyst measuring up to 65 mm with an 11 mm osseous body in the superior aspect of the cyst. Sliver of free fluid along the inferior margin of the popliteal cyst suggesting minimal recent partial rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Moderate degenerative change.
Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal horizontal oblique component of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with inferior surfacing. Fraying and blunting of the meniscal free edge.
Mild thickening of the proximal MCL compatible with remote injury.
Diffuse low grade partial-thickness chondral loss. Marginal osteophytosis.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Severe degenerative change with full-thickness chondral loss of the weightbearing and posterior portion of the compartment, with subchondral reactive marrow change. Marginal osteophytosis.
Complex degenerative multidirectional tear of the posterior horn extending into the body with significant maceration and substance loss of the body and anterior and posterior horn with minimal residual meniscal substance. There is some extrusion of the body of the lateral meniscus.
Thickened popliteus insertion with intrasubstance signal compatible with moderate tendinosis
Mildly thickened lateral collateral ligament proper which could reflect the sequela of a remote injury. Mild distal biceps tendinosis.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Degenerative changes of the anterior cruciate ligament which remains intact. The PCL is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild chondropathy. Small marginal osteophytes. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Mild edema at the suprapatellar fat pad.
Scarring at that the Hoffa's fat pad which could reflect the previous surgery-for clinical correlation.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
The intra-articular body is seen at the suprapatellar joint recess on the previous MRI is no longer present.

CONCLUSION:
1.Interval worsening of the severe osteoarthritis of the lateral compartment. Complex degenerative tearing and extensive maceration the lateral meniscus.
2.Moderate degenerative change of the medial compartment. Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus.
3.Mild degenerative change of the patellofemoral compartment.
4.Large complex popliteal cyst with an osseous body.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Severe edema of the medial condyle of left knee.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Prior MRI dated <[Date]> of <[Month]> <[YEAR]>

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intra since degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface. Findings are ready seen on prior study but appears more degenerate. Several para meniscal cysts are seen at the posterior aspect of the meniscus measuring up to 0.4 cm in size. Meniscal extrusion approximately 0.6 cm noted.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: A large subchondral cysts are seen at the posterior superior aspect of the tibial plateau, very much larger than prior study. Moderate degenerative changes multiple osteophytes are seen, most significant at the medial tibiofemoral joint. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis..

Medial compartment: Focal full-thickness chondral loss measuring up to 1.3 cm in size associated subchondral edema. Moderate chondrosis in the rest of the femoral condyle Findings have slightly progressed compared to prior study.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondral irregularity. No significant subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface, similar to previous. Interval increase in degenerative changes of the meniscus is observed. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.6 cm is seen. Multiple para meniscal cysts are also present.

Interval increase in degenerative changes are identified evident as shown by increased osteophytes, full-thickness chondral loss at the medial tibiofemoral joint associated increasing subchondral edema, and multiple enlarging subchondral cysts at the posterior medial tibial plateau.
